seo.intro1: The biggest problem for English learners isn't a lack of materials - it's a lack of a place to actually speak. You study vocabulary, grammar and listening, but without anyone to hold a real conversation with, speaking reflexes never form.
seo.intro2: Parroto solves this directly with free 1-on-1 speaking practice (voice chat) with real people. You're matched with another learner at your level (A1-C2) to talk through topics - from everyday conversation to IELTS/TOEIC Speaking practice. No more studying alone: you speak, you're heard, and natural conversation reflexes build with every chat.
seo.howTitle: How does speaking practice with real people work?
seo.howToName: How to practice English speaking online with real people on Parroto
seo.step1Desc: Choose a topic you want to talk about (everyday conversation, travel, work, IELTS Speaking…) and get matched with someone at your CEFR level.
seo.step2Desc: Join a 1-on-1 or small-group room over a voice call. Create a public or private room.
seo.step3Desc: Speak about your chosen topic with ready-made question prompts if you get stuck. The more you talk, the faster your reflexes.
seo.step4Desc: Keep your streak and join the leaderboard and community to practice speaking every day.
seo.whyTitle: Why is speaking with real people more effective?
seo.why1Desc: Pronunciation-scoring apps sharpen your accent, but only real conversation trains the think-then-speak reflex in real time.
seo.why2Desc: Speaking with someone at your level (A1-C2) keeps you from feeling overwhelmed or bored, so you speak up with more confidence.
seo.why3Desc: Rooms for IELTS Speaking, TOEIC Speaking, Business English, everyday conversation, travel and more - matched to your goal.
seo.why4Desc: A large learner community, fast matching, free to use.
seo.topicsIntro: Pick a topic that fits your goal and jump into the matching room:
seo.faqTitle: Frequently asked questions about practicing English speaking online
seo.faq1q: Is practicing English speaking with real people on Parroto free?
seo.faq1a: Yes. The voice chat speaking-practice matching is free to use - you're paired with other learners to talk through topics at your level.
seo.faq2q: Who do I get matched with?
seo.faq2a: You're matched with other learners at your CEFR level (A1-C2) who share your topic interests, so the conversation stays natural and manageable.
seo.faq3q: What if I'm shy or run out of things to say?
seo.faq3a: Every room has ready-made question and topic prompts so you never freeze up. Starting with a familiar topic and someone at your level helps you feel more confident.
seo.faq4q: Does online speaking practice help with IELTS/TOEIC Speaking?
seo.faq4a: Yes. There are dedicated IELTS Speaking and TOEIC Speaking topic rooms so you can practice the exact question formats and answering reflexes.
seo.faq5q: How many times a week should I practice speaking?
seo.faq5a: At least 3-4 sessions a week, 15-20 minutes each. Speaking consistently matters more than one long session followed by a long break.
seo.faq6q: What do I need to start practicing?
seo.faq6a: Just a phone or computer with a mic and an internet connection. Practicing shadowing first helps you speak with more confident pronunciation.

beginner.title: Beginner
beginner.description: Learners can understand familiar simple words and phrases. They need to listen repeatedly and often make mistakes when transcribing short sentences.
beginner.description_shadowing: Learners can repeat basic words and phrases but often struggle with pronunciation and timing. They need multiple listens and speak slowly.

elementary.title: Elementary
elementary.description: Learners understand simple, slow, and clear sentences on familiar topics. They can transcribe most of the content after a few listens.
elementary.description_shadowing: Learners can repeat simple sentences with clearer pronunciation. They may still pause or mispronounce unfamiliar words.

intermediate.title: Intermediate
intermediate.description: Learners can understand the main points in clearly spoken passages on common situations. They rarely need to replay and make noticeably fewer mistakes.
intermediate.description_shadowing: Learners can follow and repeat common phrases with moderate fluency. They mostly keep pace with the speaker but may lack natural intonation.

upper_intermediate.title: Upper Intermediate
upper_intermediate.description: Learners understand conversations, interviews, and news clearly with few mistakes. They can transcribe almost accurately after 1–2 listens.
upper_intermediate.description_shadowing: Learners can shadow natural-speed conversations with good fluency and rhythm. They make few mistakes and sound more confident.

dictation.title: English Listening Practice with Dictation | Parroto
dictation.description: Improve your English listening with Dictation, an expert-recommended method. Transcribe real audio and boost your listening skills with Parroto.

banner.title: English listening practice with Dictation
banner.alt: Practice English listening effectively with the Dictation method on Parroto
banner.subtitle: Enhance your English listening comprehension with the Dictation method – an effective listening practice technique recommended by experts. Start your journey to better English listening today!

intro.title: The Dictation Method Explained
intro.subtitle: Discover the most effective way to learn and refine English listening skills
intro.description: Dictation is a powerful listening practice method where you listen to native speakers and accurately transcribe what they say. This helps you grasp every word, distinguish sounds, and significantly improve overall English listening comprehension.

guide.title: Your Guide to Dictation Practice
guide.subtitle: 4 simple steps to begin your Dictation journey on Parroto

step1.title: Choose Your Lesson
step1.description: Select a lesson tailored to your proficiency level from our extensive and diverse content library. Options range from beginner conversations to advanced dialogues.
step1.alt: Screenshot of Parroto's lesson selection screen, showing various difficulty levels and topics for English dictation practice.

step2.title: Listen and Transcribe
step2.description: Listen carefully to the audio and type what you hear. You can listen multiple times, adjust playback speed, and use hints as needed to improve dictation accuracy.
step2.alt: User interface of Parroto's English dictation exercise, displaying an audio player, a text input field, and a hint button.

step3.title: Check Your Results
step3.description: Compare your transcription with the original text. Our system highlights correct and incorrect parts, helping you identify areas for improvement in listening comprehension.
step3.alt: Results screen showing a user's English dictation attempt compared to the original script, with errors highlighted for review.

step4.title: Smart Review
step4.description: The system automatically saves English words and phrases you frequently mishear or misspell. These are then added to a personalized review list for later targeted practice.
step4.alt: A smart review dashboard displaying commonly mistaken words from English dictation exercises, prompting users for further practice.

faqs.title: Frequently Asked Questions (FAQs)
faqs.subtitle: Common inquiries about the Dictation method for English listening
faqs.a1: Yes, Dictation is adaptable for all proficiency levels. You can start with foundational lessons and gradually advance the difficulty over time as your English listening skills improve.
faqs.q2: How much daily practice is recommended for Dictation?
faqs.a2: For optimal results, we suggest practicing 15-30 minutes per day. You can divide this into several shorter sessions to fit your schedule.
faqs.q3: How can I track my listening skill improvement with Dictation?
faqs.a3: The system will track your accuracy rate in exercises, identify your common mistakes, and show your progress over time through detailed analytics.
faqs.q4: Can I use Dictation on my phone?
faqs.a4: Yes, Parroto works seamlessly on any internet-connected device, including phones, tablets, and computers, allowing you to practice dictation on the go.

upper_intermediate.description_shadowing: Learners can shadow natural-speed conversations with good fluency and rhythm. They make few mistakes and sound more confident.

seo.intro1: The biggest problem for English learners isn't a lack of materials - it's a lack of a place to actually speak. You study vocabulary, grammar and listening, but without anyone to hold a real conversation with, speaking reflexes never form.
seo.intro2: Parroto solves this directly with free 1-on-1 speaking practice (voice chat) with real people. You're matched with another learner at your level (A1-C2) to talk through topics - from everyday conversation to IELTS/TOEIC Speaking practice. No more studying alone: you speak, you're heard, and natural conversation reflexes build with every chat.
seo.howTitle: How does speaking practice with real people work?
seo.howToName: How to practice English speaking online with real people on Parroto
seo.step1Desc: Choose a topic you want to talk about (everyday conversation, travel, work, IELTS Speaking…) and get matched with someone at your CEFR level.
seo.step2Desc: Join a 1-on-1 or small-group room over a voice call. Create a public or private room.
seo.step3Desc: Speak about your chosen topic with ready-made question prompts if you get stuck. The more you talk, the faster your reflexes.
seo.step4Desc: Keep your streak and join the leaderboard and community to practice speaking every day.
seo.whyTitle: Why is speaking with real people more effective?
seo.why1Desc: Pronunciation-scoring apps sharpen your accent, but only real conversation trains the think-then-speak reflex in real time.
seo.why2Desc: Speaking with someone at your level (A1-C2) keeps you from feeling overwhelmed or bored, so you speak up with more confidence.
seo.why3Desc: Rooms for IELTS Speaking, TOEIC Speaking, Business English, everyday conversation, travel and more - matched to your goal.
seo.why4Desc: A large learner community, fast matching, free to use.
seo.topicsIntro: Pick a topic that fits your goal and jump into the matching room:
seo.faqTitle: Frequently asked questions about practicing English speaking online
seo.faq1q: Is practicing English speaking with real people on Parroto free?
seo.faq1a: Yes. The voice chat speaking-practice matching is free to use - you're paired with other learners to talk through topics at your level.
seo.faq2q: Who do I get matched with?
seo.faq2a: You're matched with other learners at your CEFR level (A1-C2) who share your topic interests, so the conversation stays natural and manageable.
seo.faq3q: What if I'm shy or run out of things to say?
seo.faq3a: Every room has ready-made question and topic prompts so you never freeze up. Starting with a familiar topic and someone at your level helps you feel more confident.
seo.faq4q: Does online speaking practice help with IELTS/TOEIC Speaking?
seo.faq4a: Yes. There are dedicated IELTS Speaking and TOEIC Speaking topic rooms so you can practice the exact question formats and answering reflexes.
seo.faq5q: How many times a week should I practice speaking?
seo.faq5a: At least 3-4 sessions a week, 15-20 minutes each. Speaking consistently matters more than one long session followed by a long break.
seo.faq6q: What do I need to start practicing?
seo.faq6a: Just a phone or computer with a mic and an internet connection. Practicing shadowing first helps you speak with more confident pronunciation.

beginner.title: Beginner
beginner.description: Learners can understand familiar simple words and phrases. They need to listen repeatedly and often make mistakes when transcribing short sentences.
beginner.description_shadowing: Learners can repeat basic words and phrases but often struggle with pronunciation and timing. They need multiple listens and speak slowly.

elementary.title: Elementary
elementary.description: Learners understand simple, slow, and clear sentences on familiar topics. They can transcribe most of the content after a few listens.
elementary.description_shadowing: Learners can repeat simple sentences with clearer pronunciation. They may still pause or mispronounce unfamiliar words.

intermediate.title: Intermediate
intermediate.description: Learners can understand the main points in clearly spoken passages on common situations. They rarely need to replay and make noticeably fewer mistakes.
intermediate.description_shadowing: Learners can follow and repeat common phrases with moderate fluency. They mostly keep pace with the speaker but may lack natural intonation.

upper_intermediate.title: Upper Intermediate
upper_intermediate.description: Learners understand conversations, interviews, and news clearly with few mistakes. They can transcribe almost accurately after 1–2 listens.
upper_intermediate.description_shadowing: Learners can shadow natural-speed conversations with good fluency and rhythm. They make few mistakes and sound more confident.

advanced.title: Advanced
advanced.description: Learners understand complex speech, even with unfamiliar language. They can transcribe nearly perfectly after one listen.
advanced.description_shadowing: Learners can repeat complex sentences accurately with proper intonation and near-native fluency. They can shadow most content in real time.

proficient.title: Proficient
proficient.description: Learners fully understand and accurately transcribe complex content, including implications, nuances, and metaphors. Their skill is native-like.
proficient.description_shadowing: Learners can perfectly shadow native speakers in real time, with accurate pronunciation, rhythm, and emotion. Their speech is native-like.

intro.title: The Dictation Method Explained

intro.description: Dictation is a powerful listening practice method where you listen to native speakers and accurately transcribe what they say. This helps you grasp every word, distinguish sounds, and significantly improve overall English listening comprehension.

guide.title: Your Guide to Dictation Practice
guide.subtitle: 4 simple steps to begin your Dictation journey on Parroto

step1.title: Choose Your Lesson
step1.description: Select a lesson tailored to your proficiency level from our extensive and diverse content library. Options range from beginner conversations to advanced dialogues.
step1.alt: Screenshot of Parroto's lesson selection screen, showing various difficulty levels and topics for English dictation practice.

step2.title: Listen and Transcribe
step2.description: Listen carefully to the audio and type what you hear. You can listen multiple times, adjust playback speed, and use hints as needed to improve dictation accuracy.
step2.alt: User interface of Parroto's English dictation exercise, displaying an audio player, a text input field, and a hint button.

seo.intro1: The biggest problem for English learners isn't a lack of materials - it's a lack of a place to actually speak. You study vocabulary, grammar and listening, but without anyone to hold a real conversation with, speaking reflexes never form.
seo.intro2: Parroto solves this directly with free 1-on-1 speaking practice (voice chat) with real people. You're matched with another learner at your level (A1-C2) to talk through topics - from everyday conversation to IELTS/TOEIC Speaking practice. No more studying alone: you speak, you're heard, and natural conversation reflexes build with every chat.
seo.howTitle: How does speaking practice with real people work?
seo.howToName: How to practice English speaking online with real people on Parroto
seo.step1Desc: Choose a topic you want to talk about (everyday conversation, travel, work, IELTS Speaking…) and get matched with someone at your CEFR level.
seo.step2Desc: Join a 1-on-1 or small-group room over a voice call. Create a public or private room.
seo.step3Desc: Speak about your chosen topic with ready-made question prompts if you get stuck. The more you talk, the faster your reflexes.
seo.step4Desc: Keep your streak and join the leaderboard and community to practice speaking every day.
seo.whyTitle: Why is speaking with real people more effective?
seo.why1Desc: Pronunciation-scoring apps sharpen your accent, but only real conversation trains the think-then-speak reflex in real time.
seo.why2Desc: Speaking with someone at your level (A1-C2) keeps you from feeling overwhelmed or bored, so you speak up with more confidence.
seo.why3Desc: Rooms for IELTS Speaking, TOEIC Speaking, Business English, everyday conversation, travel and more - matched to your goal.
seo.why4Desc: A large learner community, fast matching, free to use.
seo.topicsIntro: Pick a topic that fits your goal and jump into the matching room:
seo.faqTitle: Frequently asked questions about practicing English speaking online
seo.faq1q: Is practicing English speaking with real people on Parroto free?
seo.faq1a: Yes. The voice chat speaking-practice matching is free to use - you're paired with other learners to talk through topics at your level.
seo.faq2q: Who do I get matched with?
seo.faq2a: You're matched with other learners at your CEFR level (A1-C2) who share your topic interests, so the conversation stays natural and manageable.
seo.faq3q: What if I'm shy or run out of things to say?
seo.faq3a: Every room has ready-made question and topic prompts so you never freeze up. Starting with a familiar topic and someone at your level helps you feel more confident.
seo.faq4q: Does online speaking practice help with IELTS/TOEIC Speaking?
seo.faq4a: Yes. There are dedicated IELTS Speaking and TOEIC Speaking topic rooms so you can practice the exact question formats and answering reflexes.
seo.faq5q: How many times a week should I practice speaking?
seo.faq5a: At least 3-4 sessions a week, 15-20 minutes each. Speaking consistently matters more than one long session followed by a long break.
seo.faq6q: What do I need to start practicing?
seo.faq6a: Just a phone or computer with a mic and an internet connection. Practicing shadowing first helps you speak with more confident pronunciation.

beginner.title: Beginner
beginner.description: Learners can understand familiar simple words and phrases. They need to listen repeatedly and often make mistakes when transcribing short sentences.
beginner.description_shadowing: Learners can repeat basic words and phrases but often struggle with pronunciation and timing. They need multiple listens and speak slowly.

elementary.title: Elementary
elementary.description: Learners understand simple, slow, and clear sentences on familiar topics. They can transcribe most of the content after a few listens.
elementary.description_shadowing: Learners can repeat simple sentences with clearer pronunciation. They may still pause or mispronounce unfamiliar words.

intermediate.title: Intermediate
intermediate.description: Learners can understand the main points in clearly spoken passages on common situations. They rarely need to replay and make noticeably fewer mistakes.
intermediate.description_shadowing: Learners can follow and repeat common phrases with moderate fluency. They mostly keep pace with the speaker but may lack natural intonation.

upper_intermediate.title: Upper Intermediate
upper_intermediate.description: Learners understand conversations, interviews, and news clearly with few mistakes. They can transcribe almost accurately after 1–2 listens.
upper_intermediate.description_shadowing: Learners can shadow natural-speed conversations with good fluency and rhythm. They make few mistakes and sound more confident.

advanced.title: Advanced
advanced.description: Learners understand complex speech, even with unfamiliar language. They can transcribe nearly perfectly after one listen.
advanced.description_shadowing: Learners can repeat complex sentences accurately with proper intonation and near-native fluency. They can shadow most content in real time.

proficient.title: Proficient
proficient.description: Learners fully understand and accurately transcribe complex content, including implications, nuances, and metaphors. Their skill is native-like.
proficient.description_shadowing: Learners can perfectly shadow native speakers in real time, with accurate pronunciation, rhythm, and emotion. Their speech is native-like.

banner.title: English listening practice with Dictation

banner.subtitle: Enhance your English listening comprehension with the Dictation method – an effective listening practice technique recommended by experts. Start your journey to better English listening today!

intro.title: The Dictation Method Explained
intro.subtitle: Discover the most effective way to learn and refine English listening skills
intro.description: Dictation is a powerful listening practice method where you listen to native speakers and accurately transcribe what they say. This helps you grasp every word, distinguish sounds, and significantly improve overall English listening comprehension.

guide.title: Your Guide to Dictation Practice
guide.subtitle: 4 simple steps to begin your Dictation journey on Parroto

step1.title: Choose Your Lesson
step1.description: Select a lesson tailored to your proficiency level from our extensive and diverse content library. Options range from beginner conversations to advanced dialogues.
step1.alt: Screenshot of Parroto's lesson selection screen, showing various difficulty levels and topics for English dictation practice.

step2.title: Listen and Transcribe
step2.description: Listen carefully to the audio and type what you hear. You can listen multiple times, adjust playback speed, and use hints as needed to improve dictation accuracy.
step2.alt: User interface of Parroto's English dictation exercise, displaying an audio player, a text input field, and a hint button.

step3.title: Check Your Results
step3.description: Compare your transcription with the original text. Our system highlights correct and incorrect parts, helping you identify areas for improvement in listening comprehension.
step3.alt: Results screen showing a user's English dictation attempt compared to the original script, with errors highlighted for review.

step4.title: Smart Review
step4.description: The system automatically saves English words and phrases you frequently mishear or misspell. These are then added to a personalized review list for later targeted practice.
step4.alt: A smart review dashboard displaying commonly mistaken words from English dictation exercises, prompting users for further practice.

faqs.title: Frequently Asked Questions (FAQs)
faqs.subtitle: Common inquiries about the Dictation method for English listening
faqs.a1: Yes, Dictation is adaptable for all proficiency levels. You can start with foundational lessons and gradually advance the difficulty over time as your English listening skills improve.
faqs.q2: How much daily practice is recommended for Dictation?
faqs.a2: For optimal results, we suggest practicing 15-30 minutes per day. You can divide this into several shorter sessions to fit your schedule.
faqs.q3: How can I track my listening skill improvement with Dictation?
faqs.a3: The system will track your accuracy rate in exercises, identify your common mistakes, and show your progress over time through detailed analytics.
faqs.q4: Can I use Dictation on my phone?
faqs.a4: Yes, Parroto works seamlessly on any internet-connected device, including phones, tablets, and computers, allowing you to practice dictation on the go.

beginner.title: Beginner
beginner.description: Learners can understand familiar simple words and phrases. They need to listen repeatedly and often make mistakes when transcribing short sentences.
beginner.description_shadowing: Learners can repeat basic words and phrases but often struggle with pronunciation and timing. They need multiple listens and speak slowly.

elementary.title: Elementary
elementary.description: Learners understand simple, slow, and clear sentences on familiar topics. They can transcribe most of the content after a few listens.
elementary.description_shadowing: Learners can repeat simple sentences with clearer pronunciation. They may still pause or mispronounce unfamiliar words.

intermediate.title: Intermediate
intermediate.description: Learners can understand the main points in clearly spoken passages on common situations. They rarely need to replay and make noticeably fewer mistakes.
intermediate.description_shadowing: Learners can follow and repeat common phrases with moderate fluency. They mostly keep pace with the speaker but may lack natural intonation.

upper_intermediate.title: Upper Intermediate
upper_intermediate.description: Learners understand conversations, interviews, and news clearly with few mistakes. They can transcribe almost accurately after 1–2 listens.
upper_intermediate.description_shadowing: Learners can shadow natural-speed conversations with good fluency and rhythm. They make few mistakes and sound more confident.

advanced.title: Advanced
advanced.description: Learners understand complex speech, even with unfamiliar language. They can transcribe nearly perfectly after one listen.
advanced.description_shadowing: Learners can repeat complex sentences accurately with proper intonation and near-native fluency. They can shadow most content in real time.

proficient.title: Proficient
proficient.description: Learners fully understand and accurately transcribe complex content, including implications, nuances, and metaphors. Their skill is native-like.
proficient.description_shadowing: Learners can perfectly shadow native speakers in real time, with accurate pronunciation, rhythm, and emotion. Their speech is native-like.

seo.intro1: The biggest problem for English learners isn't a lack of materials - it's a lack of a place to actually speak. You study vocabulary, grammar and listening, but without anyone to hold a real conversation with, speaking reflexes never form.
seo.intro2: Parroto solves this directly with free 1-on-1 speaking practice (voice chat) with real people. You're matched with another learner at your level (A1-C2) to talk through topics - from everyday conversation to IELTS/TOEIC Speaking practice. No more studying alone: you speak, you're heard, and natural conversation reflexes build with every chat.
seo.howTitle: How does speaking practice with real people work?
seo.howToName: How to practice English speaking online with real people on Parroto
seo.step1Desc: Choose a topic you want to talk about (everyday conversation, travel, work, IELTS Speaking…) and get matched with someone at your CEFR level.
seo.step2Desc: Join a 1-on-1 or small-group room over a voice call. Create a public or private room.
seo.step3Desc: Speak about your chosen topic with ready-made question prompts if you get stuck. The more you talk, the faster your reflexes.
seo.step4Desc: Keep your streak and join the leaderboard and community to practice speaking every day.
seo.whyTitle: Why is speaking with real people more effective?
seo.why1Desc: Pronunciation-scoring apps sharpen your accent, but only real conversation trains the think-then-speak reflex in real time.
seo.why2Desc: Speaking with someone at your level (A1-C2) keeps you from feeling overwhelmed or bored, so you speak up with more confidence.
seo.why3Desc: Rooms for IELTS Speaking, TOEIC Speaking, Business English, everyday conversation, travel and more - matched to your goal.
seo.why4Desc: A large learner community, fast matching, free to use.
seo.topicsIntro: Pick a topic that fits your goal and jump into the matching room:
seo.faqTitle: Frequently asked questions about practicing English speaking online
seo.faq1q: Is practicing English speaking with real people on Parroto free?
seo.faq1a: Yes. The voice chat speaking-practice matching is free to use - you're paired with other learners to talk through topics at your level.
seo.faq2q: Who do I get matched with?
seo.faq2a: You're matched with other learners at your CEFR level (A1-C2) who share your topic interests, so the conversation stays natural and manageable.
seo.faq3q: What if I'm shy or run out of things to say?
seo.faq3a: Every room has ready-made question and topic prompts so you never freeze up. Starting with a familiar topic and someone at your level helps you feel more confident.
seo.faq4q: Does online speaking practice help with IELTS/TOEIC Speaking?
seo.faq4a: Yes. There are dedicated IELTS Speaking and TOEIC Speaking topic rooms so you can practice the exact question formats and answering reflexes.
seo.faq5q: How many times a week should I practice speaking?
seo.faq5a: At least 3-4 sessions a week, 15-20 minutes each. Speaking consistently matters more than one long session followed by a long break.
seo.faq6q: What do I need to start practicing?
seo.faq6a: Just a phone or computer with a mic and an internet connection. Practicing shadowing first helps you speak with more confident pronunciation.
